text: And that brings us to a mistake the examiners list word for word, on the card. The question asked for the name of the hypothesis in which the active site changes shape as the substrate binds. Read this answer. Look at the words. There are two hypotheses in this lesson, and this answer has taken a piece of each and glued them together. The names can merge when both are taught together. But they are different pictures: lock-and-key is the fixed shape, induced fit is the shape that changes. The examiners' list shows five of these hybrids, and it says they were looking only for induced fit. So: two drawings, two names in your pen, lock-and-key or induced fit, never a blend of the two.
